Here is a detailed description of the provided video segment:

The video shows a woman named Amy Selikoff giving a presentation at a TEDx event in Orlando, Florida, in October 2012. She is standing on a stage with a red carpet and the TEDx logo in large red letters behind her. Amy is wearing a gray blazer, a purple top, a patterned scarf, and dark pants. She speaks directly to the audience, using hand gestures to emphasize her points. Initially, she appears with a screen behind her which transitions to various words and phrases that describe the experience of adolescence. The words appearing on the screen include “painful,” “weird,” “ambiguous,” “daring,” “smelly,” and “tumultuous.” Later, the screen displays phrases such as "survival of the fittest," "cliques," "trying to find your tribe," "rejection/acceptance," and "tessellation of feelings" with words such as rage, hope, despair, and elation. The screen transitions to display “it’s the end of the world” and then morphs to “you’re the center of the world and the universe.” Lastly, the screen displays “not a child, not an adult, you are a seeker, this makes you great.” The background of the stage is dark, but the audience can be seen sitting in the theater. Amy's expressions range from pensive to humorous as she delivers her speech. She occasionally looks down to collect her thoughts. At the end of the segment, she makes a disgusted face while talking about the struggles of that time of life.

Her speech appears to be about surviving the embarrassments of 7th grade and relating to her own experiences as a 7th-grade teacher.

The video segment features a woman with light brown hair wearing a gray blazer over a purple top and a colorful scarf giving a TEDx talk to a seated audience. She stands on a red circular platform with the word TEDx spelled out behind her in large red capital letters. The screen behind her displays a light blue background initially, then a map showing lakes. She gestures with her hands as she speaks, her expressions shifting from serious to smiling, and at times holds a small clicker in her hands. Throughout the segment, the screen behind her transitions between a blank light blue background and a map. At the moment the map is displayed on the screen, two labels are shown at "Lake Titicaca" and "Lake Poopo". During her presentation, the speaker addresses the topic of how seventh graders laugh at the geographical names of lakes. The visual transition to the map supports and enhances her point about these lake names.
